title: Six Words and a Sixty-Year Treaty
description: How ‘blood and water cannot flow together’ became a political and diplomatic doctrine The Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) of 1960 survived three full-scale wars between India and Pakistan—the 1965 war, the 1971 war, and the 1999 Kargil conflict, as well as major diplomatic crises, including the 2001 Indian Parliament attack and the 2008 Mumbai bombings.
